content.title: Planning a family meal
content.summary: Demo guide — A simple way to plan ingredients, portions and timing before cooking for visitors.
steps: Ask how many people are coming and whether anyone has food allergies or dietary needs.
Choose dishes you already know how to prepare and list the ingredients for each.
Check what you have before making a shopping list.
Write a cooking order based on the time each dish needs, leaving room for serving and cleaning.
tips: Separate items you can prepare ahead from tasks for the day.
warnings: Follow current food-safety guidance for cooking and storage.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: A smaller household can use the same checklist for a weekly meal.

content.title: Organising a market shopping list
content.summary: Demo guide — Group a shopping list by ingredient type and keep track of your spending.
steps: List the meals or household tasks you are shopping for.
Group the items into produce, dry goods and other supplies.
Set a total budget and mark which items are essential.
Record purchases as you go and review the list before leaving.
warnings: Prices and availability vary; this example does not set market prices.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: Use a paper checklist or a notes app.

content.title: Recording a family celebration
content.summary: Demo guide — Create a respectful record of a celebration through notes and consent-based interviews.
steps: Ask the organisers which parts may be recorded or shared.
Invite a willing participant to explain the event in their own words.
Write the date, place and the speaker’s preferred name.
Read your notes back to the speaker and ask what should be corrected or kept private.
tips: Record whose account you are documenting rather than claiming a universal tradition.
warnings: Do not publish private or restricted practices without permission.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: Different families may describe the same occasion differently.

content.title: Planning a community meeting
content.summary: Demo guide — Prepare an agenda and a clear way for participants to contribute.
steps: Ask participants what decisions the meeting needs to make.
Share the time, place and agenda in the group’s preferred channel.
Agree how people will take turns speaking and who will record decisions.
Read the agreed actions aloud and name the person responsible for each.
tips: Ask about accessibility and language preferences before the meeting.
warnings: This example is not a statement of any community’s formal customs.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: A small group may use an informal discussion rather than a chairperson.

content.title: Keeping household maintenance notes
content.summary: Demo guide — Keep dates, receipts and observations in one place for routine household upkeep.
steps: List the household items or areas you want to track.
Create a page for each item with its purchase date and service contact, if available.
Record maintenance dates, what was done and any follow-up agreed.
Store receipts with the matching entry and review outstanding tasks regularly.
tips: Photograph receipts if the printed text fades.
warnings: Use a qualified professional for hazardous repairs.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: A shared home can keep the log in a folder everyone can access.

content.title: Organising a shared water collection rota
content.summary: Demo guide — Agree responsibilities and keep a simple record when a household shares collection tasks.
steps: Discuss the household’s needs and the availability of each participant.
Agree who is responsible on each day and how swaps will be communicated.
Write the rota somewhere everyone can access.
Review the arrangement together when household circumstances change.
tips: Make room for participants who cannot carry heavy containers.
warnings: Water quality needs separate assessment; a rota does not make water safe to drink.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: Some households may share costs instead of collection tasks.

content.title: Preparing for a public office visit
content.summary: Demo guide — Use a checklist to organise questions and documents before visiting an office.
steps: Identify the official agency responsible for the process you need.
Check its current published requirements and opening arrangements.
Write a checklist using those official requirements and organise the requested documents.
Keep a record of the visit, any official receipt and the next action the office gives you.
tips: Date your checklist so you know when the requirements were checked.
warnings: This demo does not state current fees, eligibility or legal requirements. Verify those directly with the responsible agency.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: Some offices offer online services; use the official channel when available.

content.title: Keeping an application record
content.summary: Demo guide — Track submissions, reference numbers and follow-up dates for an administrative application.
steps: Create a folder named for the application and date.
Save a copy of the information you submitted and the official acknowledgement.
Record any reference number and the contact channel provided by the agency.
Add follow-up dates from the agency’s instructions and keep subsequent messages together.
tips: Keep reference numbers easy to find without sharing them publicly.
warnings: Do not put identity documents or sensitive personal information in a public guide.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: Use a physical folder if digital storage is not suitable.

content.title: Asking how to address someone respectfully
content.summary: Demo guide — Ask a person’s preference when you are unsure of their name, title or form of address.
steps: Introduce yourself using the name you want others to use.
Ask the person how they would like you to address them.
Listen to their answer and repeat the name if you need help with pronunciation.
Use their preference and accept a correction without making the exchange awkward.
tips: Personal preferences can differ within the same community.
warnings: Do not assume a title from someone’s appearance, age or ethnicity.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: A person may prefer a different form of address in a formal setting.

content.title: Building a personal language notebook
content.summary: Demo guide — Document phrases with a willing speaker and preserve the context in which they are used.
steps: Choose a small set of everyday situations you want to learn about.
Ask the speaker for a phrase and its meaning in each situation.
Record the speaker’s spelling or transcription preference and notes about when the phrase is appropriate.
Practise with the speaker and update your notes when they correct you.
tips: Record an audio example only with explicit permission.
warnings: This demo contains no verified translations or pronunciation claims.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: Different speakers may use different words or spellings.

content.title: Documenting a craft process
content.summary: Demo guide — Turn a demonstration into a clear sequence of notes with permission from the maker.
steps: Ask the maker which parts of the process can be documented.
List the materials and tools using the maker’s own terms.
Write one action per step while observing the demonstration.
Ask the maker to review the sequence and add important cautions before sharing it.
tips: Describe what the maker does rather than guessing why.
warnings: Get separate permission to publish photographs or commercially sensitive details.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: Some makers prefer diagrams or audio descriptions to written notes.

content.title: Organising a beginner sewing kit
content.summary: Demo guide — Keep basic tools together and make a checklist before a small sewing project.
requirements: The tools required by your chosen project
steps: Read the project instructions and list the tools they require.
Group measuring tools, marking tools and fasteners in separate compartments.
Check that reusable tools are in good condition before starting.
Return tools to their compartments and record supplies that need replacing.
tips: Start with the supplies your chosen project actually needs.
warnings: Store sharp tools securely and away from children.
sources: Local development fixture. Content and contributor confirmations are illustrative, not real community validation.
variations: A fabric pouch can replace a box for a small kit.
